crumb: Sell a Home With a Reverse Mortgage
title: Sell a House With a Reverse Mortgage in Hampton Roads, VA
description: How to sell a home with a reverse mortgage: the 95% rule for heirs, the deadlines after a borrower dies, and your options in Hampton Roads.
h1: Selling a House With a Reverse Mortgage in Hampton Roads, VA
lede: Whether you are the borrower or an heir, a reverse mortgage has rules and deadlines that change what you can do. Here is how they work, from the CFPB’s guidance.
tldr: A reverse mortgage becomes due and payable after the last borrower, co-borrower or eligible non-borrowing spouse dies. Heirs who want to sell generally must repay the full balance, or 95 percent of the appraised value if the balance is higher than the home’s value. This is general information from a real estate agent, not legal or tax advice. Talk with a Virginia attorney about your situation.

sections.h2: When a Reverse Mortgage Becomes Due
sections.html: The CFPB says a reverse mortgage becomes due and payable after the death of the borrower and of any co-borrower or eligible non-borrowing spouse. A co-borrower can usually stay in the home. An eligible non-borrowing spouse has to meet HUD criteria.

sections.h2: What Heirs Can Do, and How Much It Costs
sections.html:
To sell, heirs must repay the full loan balance, or at least 95 percent of the appraised value if the balance is more than the home is worth. If the home is worth more than the balance, the heirs sell, repay the loan and keep the difference.

That 95 percent rule matters when the home is worth less than the balance. The CFPB says the rest of the loan is covered by the mortgage insurance the borrower paid.

Once heirs receive a due and payable notice from the lender, they have 30 days to buy, sell or turn the home over. The CFPB says it may be possible to extend the timeline by up to six months so heirs can sell or get their own loan. Ask the servicer in writing what your deadline is and how to request an extension.

sections.h2: Why a Direct Sale Is Sometimes Used
sections.html:
Heirs on a deadline sometimes choose a direct sale because it is predictable, avoids repairs, and can close inside the lender’s window. If the home is in good shape, a listing may net more, so I will show you both. The servicer’s payoff letter and any approvals drive the timeline, not me.

If the borrower has died, also read about selling an inherited house, since the estate’s representative has to be able to sign.

faqs: Can I sell a house that has a reverse mortgage?
Yes. The loan is repaid from the sale. If you are the borrower, ask your servicer for a payoff statement and talk to a HUD-approved counselor.
If the balance is more than the home is worth, heirs can generally satisfy the loan by selling for at least 95 percent of the appraised value.
The CFPB says 30 days after the due and payable notice to buy, sell or turn the home over, with a possible extension of up to six months.
Does a surviving spouse have to leave?
Not necessarily. A co-borrower can usually stay. A non-borrowing spouse may qualify to stay under HUD’s rules.
What if the home needs repairs?
A direct as-is sale avoids them. Tell me the condition and your deadline.
What if the loan balance is more than the home is worth?
For a HECM, the CFPB says heirs can settle the loan by selling for at least 95 percent of the appraised value. Ask a HUD-approved counselor or attorney.
Do I need a probate case?
If the borrower died, the personal representative must be able to sign. A Virginia attorney can confirm the steps.
No. Talk with a Virginia attorney or HUD-approved counselor.
